subject: ela
intro: Good readers use phonics to decode — to figure out — unfamiliar words. In Grade 2, we learn to recognize long vowel sounds, vowel teams (two vowels that work together), r-controlled vowels, common prefixes and suffixes, and words we just have to memorize. Breaking a word into syllables and looking for familiar parts helps us read new words with confidence.

items.prompt:
Decode this word: 'mistake'. How many syllables does it have?
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3

steps: Clap the word as you say it: mis-take. Each clap is one syllable.
'mis' is the first syllable. 'take' is the second syllable.
Count the claps: 2 syllables.
solution.answer: B) 2. The word 'mistake' has two syllables: mis-take.

items.prompt:
Which word has the prefix 'un-'?
A) unhappy
B) running
C) happy

steps: A prefix is a word part added to the BEGINNING of a root word.
Look at the beginning of each word: 'un-happy', 'run-ning', 'hap-py'.
Only 'unhappy' starts with the prefix 'un-'.
'running' starts with 'run', and 'happy' has no prefix.
solution.answer: A) unhappy. The prefix 'un-' is at the beginning, attached to the root word 'happy'.

items.prompt:
What does the prefix 'un-' mean in the word 'unkind'?
A) not
B) very
C) again

steps: Think about what 'unkind' means compared to 'kind'.
If someone is kind, they are nice. If someone is unkind, they are NOT nice.
The prefix 'un-' changes a word to mean the opposite — it means 'not'.
So 'unkind' means 'not kind'.
solution.answer: A) not. The prefix 'un-' means 'not,' so 'unkind' means 'not kind'.

items.prompt:
Blend these syllables together: 'sun' + 'shine' = ___
A) sunhine
B) sunshine
C) sushine

steps: Read the first syllable: 'sun'.
Read the second syllable: 'shine'.
Put them together smoothly: 'sun' + 'shine' = 'sunshine'.
This is a compound word — two whole words joined to make a new word.
solution.answer: B) sunshine. Blending 'sun' and 'shine' makes the compound word 'sunshine'.

items.prompt:
Which word has a long vowel sound?
A) plan
B) plane
C) plop

steps: A long vowel says its own name. The vowel 'a' says 'AY' when it is long.
'plan' — the vowel 'a' is short: /pl-an/.
'plane' — the silent 'e' at the end makes the 'a' say its name: /pl-AYn/. Long vowel!
'plop' — the vowel 'o' is short: /pl-op/.
The rule: when a word ends in silent 'e', the vowel before it is usually long.
solution.answer: B) plane. The silent 'e' at the end makes the 'a' say its long sound: /pl-AYn/.

items.prompt:
Identify the root word in 'retell'.
A) re
B) tell
C) ell
items.hint: A root word is the base word before any prefix or suffix is added. The prefix 're-' means 'again.' Remove it and see what is left.

steps: The prefix 're-' means 'again' and is added to the beginning of the root word.
Remove 're-' from 'retell': you are left with 'tell'.
'tell' is a real word that makes sense on its own, so it is the root word.
solution.answer: B) tell. The root word is 'tell'. The prefix 're-' means 'again', so 'retell' means 'to tell again'.

items.prompt:
Which word has the vowel team 'ea' that makes the long /ee/ sound?
A) bread
B) dream
C) head
items.hint: Say each word aloud. In some 'ea' words the vowels say /ee/ (like 'eat'). In others, 'ea' says short /e/ (like 'bread'). Which option sounds like /ee/?

steps: The vowel team 'ea' often makes the long /ee/ sound.
'bread' — 'ea' here makes a short /e/ sound: /bred/.
'dream' — 'ea' here makes the long /ee/ sound: /dreem/. Long vowel team!
'head' — 'ea' here also makes short /e/: /hed/.
solution.answer: B) dream. The vowel team 'ea' in 'dream' makes the long /ee/ sound.

items.prompt:
Which word has an r-controlled vowel?
A) cat
B) bird
C) keep
items.hint: An r-controlled vowel is a vowel followed by the letter 'r'. The 'r' changes the vowel sound. Look for a vowel + r pattern.

steps: R-controlled vowels are vowels followed by 'r' that make a special sound.
'cat' — no 'r' after the vowel.
'bird' — the vowel 'i' is followed by 'r': the 'ir' makes the /er/ sound.
'keep' — no 'r' after the vowel.
'bird' has the r-controlled vowel pattern 'ir'.
solution.answer: B) bird. The 'ir' in 'bird' is an r-controlled vowel that makes the /er/ sound.

items.prompt:
Which suffix means 'full of' in the word 'hopeful'?
A) -ful
B) -less
C) -ness
items.hint: Think about what 'hopeful' means: full of hope. Which suffix matches that meaning?

steps: A suffix is a word part added to the END of a root word.
'-ful' means 'full of': hopeful = full of hope.
'-less' means 'without': hopeless = without hope.
'-ness' means 'the state of being': happiness = the state of being happy.
The word 'hopeful' uses the suffix '-ful', meaning 'full of'.
solution.answer: A) -ful. The suffix '-ful' means 'full of'. 'Hopeful' means 'full of hope'.

items.prompt:
Which word has an irregular spelling that you must memorize — it does NOT follow regular phonics rules?
A) jump
B) cat
C) enough
items.hint: Try sounding out each word using what you know. One word sounds very different from how it is spelled. That is the irregular word.

steps: Try sounding out each word using regular phonics:
'jump' — /j/ /u/ /m/ /p/ — sounds exactly as spelled. Regular.
'cat' — /k/ /a/ /t/ — sounds exactly as spelled. Regular.
'enough' — if you sound it out, it might seem like 'en-off'. The 'gh' makes an /f/ sound, which is irregular.
'enough' is a sight word — its spelling does not follow regular rules.
solution.answer: C) enough. The word 'enough' has an irregular spelling. The '-ough' part makes the /uf/ sound, which must be memorized.
